non_claim: Every weight, loss and cost below is an illustrative model hypothesis chosen to make one contract behaviour checkable by hand. None is a measurement, a calibrated probability or an empirical claim about any repository.

scenarios.question: Which module defines an identifier the agent already knows by name?
scenarios.expected_behaviour: An exact search is cheap and decisive, so it is proposed before any decision; an empty result keeps the residual world alive and ends in abstention, never in a guessed edit.

scenarios.question: Where is a behaviour handled when the request and the code share no vocabulary?
scenarios.expected_behaviour: A literal search on the request's own words has a constant outcome and is never proposed; a structural walk is proposed only when the budget affords it, otherwise the controller abstains.

scenarios.question: Is a change safe when a dependent may be wired through a registry instead of a direct reference?
scenarios.expected_behaviour: An empty direct-reference result is not proof of absence; the observation that discriminates the critical omission is proposed first.

scenarios.question: May a change be applied when the rule that governs it is written nowhere in the source?
scenarios.expected_behaviour: Source reads cannot discriminate the requirement; the change stays inadmissible until the authored requirement is observed, whatever its expected loss.

scenarios.question: What happens when two observations agree with no declared world?
scenarios.expected_behaviour: The second observation is refused outside the model and the prior state is left unchanged; nothing is renormalised across bad options.

scenarios.question: What does the controller return when it can afford no observation, or runs out of its own search budget?
scenarios.expected_behaviour: It stops on the best admissible decision, reports every probe as unaffordable without inventing a value, and labels a truncated search as not exact.
